title: Sir Gourdon Squash
desc: A butternut gentleman who arrived at the Autumn Ball by mistake and stayed for the canapés. He polishes his monocle whenever a conversation turns awkward, which is always. Rumour says he once proposed to a soup tureen, mistaking it for a duchess in a very round hat.

title: Madame Teabite
desc: A spider tea sommelier with eight legs and eight teacups—none of them ever empty. She refuses to serve coffee “on principle” and judges every guest by how they hold the saucer. Her lace bonnet was spun at three in the morning during a particularly strong oolong.

title: Lady Slugworth
desc: The Baron's distant cousin from the damp side of the garden. She wears a tiara of dew drops, a necklace of very slow pearls, and never arrives anywhere on time—she simply makes an entrance. Every trail she leaves sparkles, and she expects compliments for it.

title: Buzzby Caramello
desc: A candy-corn bee who mistook espresso for nectar and has been vibrating ever since. Buzzby delivers sweets to every door on the street in under four minutes, then forgets which street. Do not call him on the phone—he will answer, panic, and hang up mid-buzz.

title: Count Hopula
desc: A fluffy vampire bunny who only drinks carrot juice—freshly squeezed, with a bendy straw, at midnight sharp. He flaps his bat wings mostly for drama; he actually gets around by hopping. Lactose makes him faint, so please, no carrot cake with cream cheese.

title: Ghostina Gravy
desc: A ghost chef who has been stirring the same Eternal Soup for 200 years—it is almost ready. She tastes it every hour, sighs dramatically, and adds one more pinch of salt. The kitchen mirror is covered with a towel: she claims her reflection keeps stealing the croutons.

title: Toad Mortimer
desc: A retired grim reaper toad who traded his scythe for a very large dinner fork. He still wears the hood out of habit and sleeps through most of the haunting season. Whenever he takes a nap, he feels guilty about it—and then takes another nap to recover.

title: Haunted Garlic Braid
desc: Nobody planted this garlic—it simply grew one night in the attic, already braided. A tiny ghost lives between the cloves and hums lullabies to them. Hang it by the door to chase away glitches, vampires, and anyone you didn't want to invite anyway.

title: Moody Ring
desc: A ring with a little storm cloud trapped inside the stone. On good days it sulks and does nothing. On bad days it rains a little, hugs your finger, and gives you strength—because misery loves company, and this ring loves you.

title: Spool Ghoul
desc: A grumpy wooden spool who was wound too tight in 1893 and never relaxed since. She keeps a needle tucked in her thread “for emergencies” and gossips with the buttons about the scissors. Small, cross, and surprisingly helpful when something comes apart.

title: Caramel Onion
desc: It looks exactly like a caramel apple. It is not a caramel apple. One bite brings tears, regret, and a strange sense of strength. The onion knows what it did and smirks about it from under its sweet disguise.

title: Bat Boba
desc: Cherry bubble tea with tiny bat-shaped pearls that flap around your mouth. Best enjoyed after midnight, when the bats are most awake and the straw is most dramatic. Do not shake—they get dizzy.

title: Fang Floss
desc: Mint dental floss for those with very pointy smiles. It cleans fangs, untangles bad memories, and removes small glitches stuck between reality and your teeth. A little painful, but a vampire must look fresh.

title: Mystery Stew
desc: Cooked only once a year from whatever was left in the cupboard and one thing that was looking back. Every spoonful is different: warm and cozy, or slightly cursed. The bowl itself is not sure what is inside.

title: Pumpkin Scooter
desc: A taxi scooter on two glowing pumpkin wheels—cheaper than a broom, faster than a ghost. It drives you anywhere you want, as long as it's away from your chores. Riders report a mysterious lack of guilt about skipping work.

title: Ghost Thimble
desc: An old silver thimble with a shy ghost living inside. Every time it's used, the ghost whispers, “Again me?”—and then helps anyway. It refuses to look in mirrors, which is a problem for a shiny object.
